SMTO-EXE-0237 — Your Docker cleanup list is out of date

GUID: 29976154-e7fd-5dfc-abb3-20deaa079506
Slug: docker-prune-preview-stale
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: docker

What happened

  • SMTO stopped the cleanup because the list of items to delete was too old or things in Docker changed after you reviewed it. Anything already deleted before the change stays deleted; nothing else was removed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In this conversation, ask SMTO to make a new Docker cleanup preview for the same kinds of items. Each preview can be used only once and expires after five minutes, so the old one can no longer be used.
  2. Read the new list carefully and check it only contains things you are happy to delete. Items may have changed since the first preview, so the new list is the one that counts.
  3. Approve the cleanup within five minutes, and avoid starting or stopping containers on that Gateway in the meantime. Any change to Docker between the preview and the deletion makes the list out of date again.

What success looks like

  • The cleanup finishes and SMTO reports the items it removed from the new preview.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway computer. Don't run broad Docker cleanup commands by hand to get around this; they can delete things the preview was designed to protect.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Docker prune request on the Gateway used a preview token that was missing, expired (previews last five minutes), already used, or no longer matched the current containers, images, networks, volumes or build cache.

What this means

  • A prune preview token was absent, expired or already consumed, or current object inventory/revisions changed before or during deletion. Completed deletions remain retained individually. Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.

Why this can happen

  • A prune preview token was absent, expired or already consumed, or current object inventory/revisions changed before or during deletion. Completed deletions remain retained individually.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect original preview token, current inventory and known_completed removals before making a fresh plan.

How to fix it

  • Request a new docker.prune_preview (or docker.volume_prune_preview), review its exact candidates, and submit docker.prune / docker.volume_prune / docker.volume_remove with that new preview_token and exactly the same categories within 300 seconds. Previews are single-use and do not survive a Gateway restart; avoid concurrent external Docker administration during cleanup.
  • Obtain a new preview or resolved Compose revision and confirm the exact changed scope.

Retry and execution caution

  • Obtain a new preview or resolved Compose revision and confirm the exact changed scope.

How to verify the fix

  • A new exact preview reflects remaining eligible objects and current revisions without replaying completed removals.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay an uncertain Docker mutation.

Technical notes

  • Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
